title: Bowtie compression is common in biochemical, bioelectric and mechanical pathways

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Bowtie compression is common in biochemical, bioelectric and mechanical pathways

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Levin argues that a bowtie architecture, which compresses data to a generative kernel that must later be re-inflated and reinterpreted, is common at the subcellular scale in biochemical, bioelectrical and biomechanical pathways, as well as in the egg stage of the metazoan life cycle and in learning.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 4. Beyond the Brain: Bowties Everywhere

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Note that this bowtie architecture—which forces a compression36 of data to a generative kernel that then has to be re-inflated and elaborated—is also a common feature of biochemical, bioelectrical, and biomechanical pathways (Figure 7), that is, at the subcellular scale;

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2024), doi:10.3390/e26060481; section “4. Beyond the Brain: Bowties Everywhere”. Scope: Subcellular signalling pathways and metazoan life cycles

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-memory-09: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Network topology is measurable and substantial public pathway data exist. Coverage is biased toward biochemical pathways, and enrichment can depend strongly on representation choices, so only part of the broad claim is currently resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define bowtie topology as many inputs converging on a smaller core and diverging to many outputs, then estimate this structure in curated biochemical, bioelectric and mechanical networks and compare its prevalence with degree-preserving null networks. Significant enrichment across all pathway classes supports the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Bowtie definitions and network boundaries are analyst-dependent.

Bioelectric and biomechanical networks are less comprehensively curated.

The egg and learning extensions require different data types.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.35
data existence: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.4
analysis feasibility: 0.4

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Biochemical pathway databases are public and can be scored, with standard graph methods, for an hourglass or bowtie shape. That covers only part of the stated scope: bioelectrical and biomechanical pathways are sparsely mapped, and the claim also includes the egg stage and learning. Competing definitions of the waist make the test informative but not clean, so the claim is only partly resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On public pathway maps, score each network for a narrow intermediate layer that many inputs converge on and that many outputs diverge from. A high rate of that topology in biochemical, bioelectric, and biomechanical maps would support the claim; restriction to a few metabolic networks would refute the claim that the architecture is common across those classes.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Formal definitions of a bowtie disagree on how narrow the waist must be.

The egg-stage and learning cases are not in these pathway databases.

Bioelectric and biomechanical processes are poorly represented relative to metabolic pathways.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.6
data existence: 0.75
discriminating power: 0.45
operationalizability: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.45
